t: 3615. Longest Palindromic Path in Graph — Editorial
o:
## Understanding the problem
Find a simple path (no repeated nodes) in an undirected labeled graph whose label sequence is a palindrome; maximize its length. n ≤ 14 immediately suggests bitmask DP over node subsets. Example 3: path 0→3→1 spells 'b','c','b' — a palindrome of length 3.

Key observation: a palindrome path is symmetric — it grows outward from its center by attaching matching-character neighbors to either end. So a state only needs the visited set and the two endpoints.
k: n ≤ 14 permits states (mask, endpoint1, endpoint2): ~2¹⁴·14² ≈ 3.2M states.
A path with node set mask and endpoints i, j has a palindromic label sequence; it extends by neighbor k of i (or j) not in mask iff label[k] equals the opposite endpoint's label.
Answer is the maximum popcount(mask) over all reachable states; single nodes give baseline 1.

a.n: Approach 1: Bitmask reachability over (mask, i, j)
a.i: Enumerate all base states: single nodes (mask={i}, i==i) and adjacent pairs with equal labels. Repeatedly expand: from (mask, i, j), for each neighbor k of i outside mask with label[k]==label[j], add state (mask|k, k, j); symmetrically for j. Every palindrome path is built this way from its center outward, so reachability exploration finds the maximum mask size.
s: Seed states: (1<<i, i, i) for all i; (mask(u,v), u, v) for edges with label[u]==label[v].
BFS/DFS expansion as described, tracking visited states in a set.
Track and return the maximum popcount encountered.
a.t: O(2ⁿ · n² · n) worst case — each of ~2ⁿ·n² states expands over n neighbors; n ≤ 14 keeps this fast.
a.sp: O(2ⁿ · n²) for the visited-state set.

w: This bitmask-endpoint DP is essentially the only tractable design at n = 14. Pitfalls: seeding two-node states (an edge alone with equal labels is a palindrome of length 2), remembering a single node is a length-1 palindrome, and deduplicating states (the same mask/endpoints can be reached many ways). Follow-up: count palindromic paths, or handle labeled directed graphs.
